Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: South Africa operates a partially deployed nationwide digital ID system. The Smart ID card (introduced 2013) has been issued to over 25 million citizens as of end 2024/25. However, millions still hold the older green bar-coded ID book, which is being phased out. A fully functional 'Digital ID' (app-based, remote authentication) was announced for launch in 2026 by President Ramaphosa, with the MyMzansi DPI roadmap targeting 90% Smart ID uptake by 2028. System is partially deployed but not yet fully nationwide in digital form.
